Q: Raspberry Pi 5 IR error: Protocols for device cannot be changed, unable to attach bpf program, lirc device name was not found A:

I found the answer by executing ir-keytable with no parameters, to list all devices:

$ sudo ir-keytable
Found /sys/class/rc/rc1/ with:
    Name: vc4-hdmi-1
    Driver: cec
    Default keymap: rc-cec
    Input device: /dev/input/event3
    Supported kernel protocols: cec 
    Enabled kernel protocols: cec 
    bus: 30, vendor/product: 0000:0000, version: 0x0001
    Repeat delay: 0 ms, repeat period: 125 ms
Found /sys/class/rc/rc2/ with:
    Name: gpio_ir_recv
    Driver: gpio_ir_recv
    Default keymap: rc-rc6-mce
    Input device: /dev/input/event5
    LIRC device: /dev/lirc0
    Attached BPF protocols: xbox_dvd
    Supported kernel protocols: lirc rc-5 rc-5-sz jvc sony nec sanyo mce_kbd rc-6 sharp xmp imon 
    Enabled kernel protocols: lirc rc-5 rc-5-sz jvc sony nec sanyo mce_kbd rc-6 sharp xmp imon 
    bus: 25, vendor/product: 0001:0001, version: 0x0100
    Repeat delay: 500 ms, repeat period: 125 ms
Found /sys/class/rc/rc0/ with:
    Name: vc4-hdmi-0
    Driver: cec
    Default keymap: rc-cec
    Input device: /dev/input/event1
    Supported kernel protocols: cec 
    Enabled kernel protocols: cec 
    bus: 30, vendor/product: 0000:0000, version: 0x0001
    Repeat delay: 0 ms, repeat period: 125 ms

Notice there are 3 devices found, and the one I'm interested in is rc2 (/dev/lirc0). The error was coming not from this device, but from the device rc0 that ir-keytable grabs as default.

Specifying the rc2 as the device I want to listen events for, solves the problem:

$ sudo ir-keytable -t -p all -s rc2
Protocols changed to unknown other lirc rc-5 rc-5-sz jvc sony nec sanyo mce_kbd rc-6 sharp xmp cec imon rc-mm 
Loaded BPF protocol xbox-dvd
Testing events. Please, press CTRL-C to abort.
1428.304014: lirc protocol(necx): scancode = 0xeac22a
1428.304021: event type EV_MSC(0x04): scancode = 0xeac22a
1428.304021: event type EV_SYN(0x00).
1428.412007: lirc protocol(necx): scancode = 0xeac2aa
1428.412014: event type EV_MSC(0x04): scancode = 0xeac2aa
1428.412014: event type EV_SYN(0x00).
1428.524011: lirc protocol(necx): scancode = 0xe0c032
1428.524023: event type EV_MSC(0x04): scancode = 0xe0c032
1428.524023: event type EV_SYN(0x00).

You can use this free self hosted app http://infinitewp.com No limitation in number of sites being managed. You can update WP/plugin/themes, do backups, one click login to your WordPress admin panel.

Q: How to pull latest updates from GitHub to local? A:

# Step 1: Open your terminal or Git Bash (or use Visual Studio's integrated terminal)

# Step 2: Navigate to your project directory

cd path/to/your/project

# Step 3: Ensure you're in the correct branch (if necessary)

git branch # Check which branch you're on

git checkout branch-name # Switch to the branch you need, if necessary

# Step 4: Pull the latest updates from the repository

git pull origin branch-name

# Step 5: If you haven't cloned the repository yet, use this command:

git clone https://github.com/username/repository-name.git

Q: How to resolve "Bundle Version Must Be Higher" error when uploading React Native Expo app to Transporter? A:

Increasing version number by one (from 1.0.6 to 1.0.7) fixed this for me.
